articles.title: Ethan Ebanks-Landell Prepares for Crawley Town Clash
articles.excerpt: Rochdale AFC captain Ethan Ebanks-Landell discusses the upcoming match against Crawley Town, highlighting the team's focus and determination to secure a victory at home.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale AFC captain Ethan Ebanks-Landell has expressed confidence ahead of Saturday's home match against Crawley Town. He emphasised the importance of the game for the team's aspirations this season.

Ebanks-Landell noted that the squad has been working hard in training and is eager to translate that effort into a strong performance on the pitch.

The match is set to take place at the Crown Oil Arena, and fans are encouraged to support the team as they aim for a crucial three points in the league.

Following this fixture, Rochdale will look to build momentum as they continue their campaign, urging supporters to create a vibrant atmosphere to inspire the players.

Smith & Britannia Metals have announced the extension of their sponsorship agreement with Rochdale AFC for the upcoming season. This partnership underscores the company's commitment to local sports and community engagement.

The renewed sponsorship will feature Smith & Britannia Metals' branding prominently at Spotland Stadium and on the team's kits, strengthening ties with the club's supporters.

articles.title: Rochdale Council Set to Approve £20 Million Funding for Local Improvements
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council is expected to accept nearly £20 million in government funding aimed at revitalising historically overlooked areas, including Hurstead, Smallbridge, and Belfield, at a meeting on August 25.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Council is poised to approve nearly £20 million in government funding aimed at revitalising underinvested areas of the borough. The funding, known as the Pride in Place initiative, totals £19.6 million and will be allocated over the next decade, providing just under £2 million annually for targeted improvements.

The areas set to benefit from this funding include Hurstead, Smallbridge, and Belfield, which have historically received little investment. At a town hall meeting scheduled for August 25, council leaders will also establish the Hurstead, Smallbridge and Belfield Neighbourhood Board, responsible for developing a proposal on how to utilise the funds effectively. This board will include local community representatives, Rochdale MP Paul Waugh, and the council's regeneration lead, Councillor Daniel Meredith, with Laura Rodwell of the M6 Theatre group serving as chair.

While no specific plans have been finalised, early suggestions for the funding's use include tackling congestion, improving parking, creating new green spaces, enhancing local facilities, and expanding maternity services. The Neighbourhood Board is tasked with submitting a four-year plan to the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government by November 30, 2026, to unlock the funding. An initial £150,000 has already been granted to establish the board and develop the plan.

Local residents have expressed a mix of skepticism and hope regarding the funding. Ken Whittle, a long-time resident, noted the area's neglect and emphasised the need for community facilities and social housing. Another resident, Dinah Banks, highlighted the lack of local health services and called for improvements. MP Paul Waugh has engaged with the community to gather input on their needs, ensuring that local voices will shape the future of the initiative.

articles.title: Lift at Derker Tram Stop Out of Service Until Further Notice
articles.excerpt: The lift at Derker tram stop is currently out of service, affecting access for passengers travelling towards and away from Manchester. Alternative step-free access routes are available.
articles.content_html:
The lift at Derker tram stop is out of service as of 20 August 2026, with no specified date for repairs. This disruption affects passengers using the tram service in both directions.

For those travelling towards Manchester, step-free access can be achieved via a ramp from Cromford Street directly to the Manchester-bound platform. Passengers heading towards Rochdale can also use a ramp from Cromford Street, followed by a track crossing to reach the Rochdale-bound platform.

Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has apologised for any inconvenience caused by this disruption and is advising passengers to use the alternative routes provided.

Updates regarding the lift's status will be communicated through the Bee Network live travel alerts. Passengers are encouraged to check for further information before travelling.

articles.title: Demolition of Regent Mill in Heywood to Facilitate Housing Regeneration
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council plans to demolish Regent Mill on St James Street to pave the way for new housing, potentially adding 200 affordable homes to Heywood.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Council has announced plans to demolish Regent Mill, an industrial complex located on St James Street in Heywood, as part of a broader regeneration initiative for the area. The demolition is expected to unlock opportunities for the construction of around 200 new homes, primarily aimed at providing affordable housing for local residents.

Councillor Danny Meredith, cabinet member for regeneration and housing, stated that the demolition is a key component of the council's masterplan to transform brownfield sites around Heywood town centre. He emphasised the importance of replacing the deteriorating mill with high-quality social homes to address the local housing shortage and enhance the visual appeal of the area.

The council has not yet provided a timeline for the demolition or subsequent housing development. However, the project is part of a wider £20 million investment from the government's Pride in Place funding, which aims to improve local infrastructure and support businesses in the region. Recent improvements in Heywood town centre, including the completion of a new civic building and enhancements to Peine Square, are also part of this regeneration effort.

While the demolition is anticipated to bring positive changes, there are concerns from highways teams regarding potential damage to road surfaces during the process. Planning documents indicate that the site will be secured with fencing and debris netting to ensure pedestrian safety during the demolition.

articles.title: Oulder Hill Leadership Academy Achieves Highest GCSE Results in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Oulder Hill Leadership Academy has reported a record 50% of pupils achieving grades 9 to 5 in English and Mathematics in this year's GCSE results, highlighting the school's academic success.
articles.content_html:
Oulder Hill Leadership Academy in Rochdale has announced that 50% of its pupils achieved grades 9 to 5 in both English and Mathematics in this year's GCSE results. This marks the highest proportion of students reaching these benchmarks in the school's history, with 67% securing grades 9 to 4 in the two subjects.

Among the top-performing students is Fatima Fahad, who achieved four grade 9s, five grade 8s, and a Level 2 Distinction. Fatima, who received the Academic Excellence Award at the Rochdale Encouraging You Awards earlier this year, plans to study Mathematics, Chemistry, and Computer Science at Rochdale Sixth Form. Her father praised the school's supportive environment, noting the positive impact of its recent transition to Star Academies.

Other notable achievements include Spencer Blackband, who secured three grade 8s and a grade 7 in Mathematics, and Head Girl Veronica Asnani, who achieved four grade 8s and two grade 7s. Both students will continue their education at Rochdale Sixth Form. Deputy Head Boy Michael Tarran also excelled, achieving one grade 9 and six grade 8s, while Manahil Shaban, who joined the school in Year 10, achieved a grade 9 in Urdu and five grade 8s.

Principal Adi Smale expressed pride in the students' accomplishments, stating that their results reflect their resilience and ambition. He highlighted the dedication of the staff and the support from families and the wider community. The school has also been recognised with a Silver award in the Making a Difference Secondary School of the Year category at the Pearson National Teaching Awards, with 99% of its pupils progressing to positive destinations after graduation.

articles.title: Rochdale Commemorates Comedian Jimmy Cricket Ahead of Funeral
articles.excerpt: Rochdale will pay tribute to comedian Jimmy Cricket, who passed away on August 3, with a vigil and funeral service this week.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale will have the opportunity to remember legendary comedian Jimmy Cricket ahead of his funeral this week. Jimmy Cricket, known for his clean humour and catchphrase 'And there’s more', died on August 3 at the age of 80 after a short illness, surrounded by family.

His body will lie in state at St Patrick’s Catholic Church in Rochdale on Thursday, August 20, from 3pm to 5pm for those wishing to pay their respects. Following this, a vigil mass will take place at Salford Cathedral at 7pm, marking the reception of his body.

The funeral service is scheduled for 1.30pm on Friday, August 21, at Salford Cathedral. Mourners are encouraged to wear bow ties, which, along with his trademark Wellington boots, became synonymous with the beloved entertainer.

Jimmy Cricket was a prominent figure in the comedy scene during the 1970s and was a dedicated supporter of local charities and causes in Rochdale, where he resided.

articles.title: Strike Planned by Staff at Rochdale Infirmary and Three Other Greater Manchester Hospitals
articles.excerpt: Hundreds of staff, including nurses and support workers, are set to strike at Rochdale Infirmary and three other hospitals over a dispute regarding overtime management.
articles.content_html:
Hundreds of operating theatre staff are preparing to strike at Rochdale Infirmary and three other Greater Manchester hospitals next week. The strike, involving more than 350 employees including nurses, clinical support workers, and housekeepers, is scheduled for Monday 24 August, Wednesday 26 August, and Friday 28 August.

The dispute centres on the Northern Care Alliance Foundation Trust's (NCA) use of an outside agency, NHS Professionals (NHSP), to manage overtime. Trade union Unison claims that an offer made by NCA to resolve the issue was withdrawn before discussions could take place. Kevin Dolan, a regional organiser for Unison, expressed frustration over the situation, stating that staff are merely asking for what their contracts entitle them to.

Gertie Nic Philib, the trust's chief people and strategy officer, acknowledged the staff's right to take lawful industrial action but did not provide further details on the negotiations. Dolan added that the leadership at NCA has shown a lack of commitment to resolving the dispute, which he believes could be easily addressed through continued negotiations.

The strikes may disrupt services at Rochdale Infirmary and the other affected hospitals, including Salford Royal Hospital, Royal Oldham Hospital, and Fairfield Hospital in Bury. Patients and families are advised to check for updates regarding any changes to scheduled procedures during this period.

articles.title: Cardinal Langley RC High School Reports Significant Increase in GCSE and BTEC Results
articles.excerpt: Students at Cardinal Langley RC High School in Rochdale celebrate improved GCSE and BTEC results, with notable achievements among the top performers. Over 100 students will continue their studies at the school's Sixth Form.
articles.content_html:
Students at Cardinal Langley RC High School in Rochdale are celebrating a significant rise in their GCSE and BTEC results this year. The school reported that 54.2% of all grades achieved were grade 5 or above, marking an increase of 10.6 percentage points from the previous year. Additionally, 19.2% of grades were grade 7 or above, which is an improvement of 6.2 percentage points.

Among the standout performers was a student named Conrad, who achieved an impressive seven grade 9s, two grade 8s, a grade 7, and a Distinction*. He plans to continue his studies at Cardinal Langley’s Sixth Form. Other high achievers include Charlie, who received four grade 9s and will study History, Politics, and Maths, and Daniela, who achieved three grade 9s and will pursue Maths, Biology, Chemistry, and Spanish.

The school has reported that more than 100 students have enrolled to continue their education at Cardinal Langley’s Sixth Form, where they will begin their A level studies. Other notable results include Grace, who achieved three grade 9s and will study English Literature, Biology, and Geography, and Finn, who received three grade 9s and six grade 7s, planning to study English Language, English Literature, History, and Politics.

The rise in results reflects the hard work and dedication of both students and staff at Cardinal Langley RC High School. The school community is looking forward to supporting these students as they embark on their A level studies, which will begin shortly.
